title: The Night Before the Conquest
subtitle: Ten Thousand Fires at Marr al-Zahran, the Encounter of Abu Sufyan, and the Proclamation of Peace
summary: On the eve of the entry into Makkah, the valley of Marr al-Zahran was illuminated by ten thousand individual campfires, creating a display of overwhelming strength designed to shatter Makkan resistance without bloodshed. Intercepted while scouting the perimeter, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb was escorted by Al-Abbas into the presence of the Prophet, where he embraced Islam. In an act of consummate statesmanship, the Prophet issued his famous three-fold guarantee of security.

sections.text: A Sea of Fire in the Desert Valley

As darkness descended upon the encampment at Marr al-Zahran on the nineteenth of Ramadan, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered a masterful psychological maneuver designed to avert armed resistance. He commanded every single warrior among the ten thousand to kindle his own individual campfire upon the valley floor and across the surrounding ridges. Within an hour, the dark mountainous landscape was transformed into a dazzling, roaring sea of ten thousand blazing fires, stretching across miles of desert terrain.

Inside Makkah, rumors of suspicious movements had plunged the leadership of Quraysh into extreme distress. Anxious to ascertain the truth, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb slipped out of the city under cover of night accompanied by Hakim ibn Hizam and Budayl ibn Warqa' to scout the northern passes. Ascending an elevation overlooking Marr al-Zahran, Abu Sufyan stopped dead in his tracks, horrified by the boundless panorama of campfires illuminating the night sky.

Staring at the flames in disbelief, Abu Sufyan asked: 'What is this? I have never seen such fires and encampments even during the great gatherings of Arafat!' Budayl suggested: 'These must be the fires of the tribes of Khuza'ah stirred for war.' But Abu Sufyan retorted: 'Khuza'ah is far too small and humiliated to field such fires and armies!'

Meanwhile, Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib had ridden out on the Prophet's white mule, Al-Baghla, searching for woodcutters or travelers whom he might send to warn Quraysh to surrender before the army marched into their sanctuary. Hearing Abu Sufyan's familiar voice in the darkness, Al-Abbas called out: 'O Abu Hanzalah!' Abu Sufyan recognized him immediately: 'Is that Abu al-Fadl?' Al-Abbas answered: 'Yes! Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among ten thousand men! By Allah, if he enters Makkah by force tomorrow, it will be the ruin of Quraysh!'

Terrified, Abu Sufyan pleaded: 'What is the recourse, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you?' Al-Abbas told him to mount behind him on the mule, riding straight into the Muslim camp under his personal protection. As they passed the sentry fires, Umar ibn al-Khattab caught sight of Abu Sufyan and shouted: 'Abu Sufyan! The enemy of Allah! Praise be to Allah who has delivered you without pact or covenant!' Umar hurried to the Prophet's tent seeking permission to execute him, but Al-Abbas intervened: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have granted him protection!'
The Dawn Reconciliation and Embracing of Islam

The Prophet commanded Al-Abbas to host Abu Sufyan for the night and bring him back at dawn. When morning broke, Abu Sufyan observed the ten thousand warriors performing the dawn prayer in perfect, unified ranks behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, moving in profound reverence as one body. Overwhelmed by this spiritual discipline, Abu Sufyan was brought before the Prophet.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed him with gentle magnanimity: 'Woe to you, O Abu Sufyan! Has the time not come for you to know that there is no god but Allah?' Abu Sufyan replied: 'How noble, clement, and generous in kinship you are! By Allah, I have realized that had there been any other god beside Him, he would have aided me before today.' The Prophet then asked: 'Has the time not come for you to know that I am the Messenger of Allah?' After a moment of hesitation, urged by Al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan declared his testimony of faith: 'I bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.'
The Historic Proclamation of General Safety

Recognizing the aristocratic psychology of the Makkan leader, Al-Abbas whispered to the Prophet: 'O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a man who loves honor and distinction, so grant him something.' In an act of supreme political and spiritual statesmanship, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ issued a sweeping declaration of amnesty that transformed potential battle into peaceful capitulation:

مَنْ دَخَلَ دَارَ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ فَهُوَ آمِنٌ، وَمَنْ أَلْقَى السِّلاَحَ فَهُوَ آمِنٌ، وَمَنْ أَغْلَقَ بَابَهُ فَهُوَ آمِنٌ
'Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe; whoever lays down his weapons is safe; and whoever locks his door is safe.' (Sahih Muslim 1780; Sunan Abi Dawud 3021)

To cement this reality, the Prophet instructed Al-Abbas to station Abu Sufyan at the narrow gorge of the mountain pass at Dhu Tuwa so he could witness the majestic military squadrons of Islam marching past. Squadron after squadron filed through under tribal banners, culminating in the green armored brigade of the Prophet surrounded by the Muhajirun and Ansar. Shaken to his core, Abu Sufyan turned to Al-Abbas and remarked: 'O Abbas, the dominion of your nephew has become mighty!' Al-Abbas replied: 'O Abu Sufyan, it is not mere dominion; it is prophethood!' Abu Sufyan answered: 'Then yes, indeed.'

Abu Sufyan rushed frantically ahead into Makkah, screaming at the top of his lungs through the streets: 'O people of Quraysh! Muhammad has come upon you with a force you cannot resist! Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever locks his door is safe, and whoever enters the Mosque is safe!' The citizens dropped their weapons and rushed inside their homes, sealing the fate of the city before a single soldier stepped within its walls.
